jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
We are hiring an Executive Director who is accountable for the diligent planning, organizing, and energizing of staff, services, and programs to foster a vibrant environment for residents. Ensures strict adherence to regulations concerning resident care, safety, and rights protection. Key responsibilities encompass personnel oversight, culture cultivation, effective communication strategies, financial stewardship, admissions processes, operational best practices, strategic planning, administration, and rigorous quality assurance measures. Will act as the licensed nursing home administrator or delegate under the Administrator's guidance.
What You Will Do:* Works collaboratively with Sequoia Living Support Services (Home Office) and other CCRC/LifePlan locations to identify and implement best practices, unifying where able across all locations.
* Leads and cultivates a positive culture where staff and residents are encouraged to respectfully identify ways we can improve while exhibiting the values of accountability, caring, and teamwork.
* Establishes goals and objectives consistent with mission statements and corporate goals, objectives, and policies. Assures that plans and actions reflect board goals and objectives.
* Develops long term plans, including operation plans, capital plans, major projects, improvements, staffing needs, programs and services.
* Responsible for implementing appropriate corporate policy; makes recommendations for new policies and procedures with staff.
* Performs duties related to staffing including recruiting, screening, hiring, training, orientation, development, evaluation, and motivation of employees.
* Implements plans to achieve performance indicators and dashboard targets.
* Manages the financials including budget development and analysis, administration and forecasting.
* Collaborates with resident leadership and related committees to ensure smooth implementation of community goals and positive resident relations.
* Member of the senior management team. Participates at the corporate level in task forces and committees as required or assigned.
* Serves as Community Risk Manager, overseeing loss prevention and control activities for the entire community under the auspices of the Corporate Risk Management Program.
* Responsible for implementing Safety, Accident and Illness Prevention Program at site. Coordinates Safety Committee.
* Maintains liaison with government agencies, service agencies, neighborhood committees, volunteers, and other professional and supervisory staff.
* Participates in staff development for future continuity and succession planning.
* Performs other work as assigned.


Why Work Here:* For individuals who work more than 30 hrs/week, employer\-paid medical, dental \& vision, 18 days PTO \+ 8 holidays, 403(b) with employer contribution, tuition assistance, referral bonuses, employee discounts, and growth opportunities.


Who You Are:
* Knowledge of Title 22, OBRA and policies and procedures related to the operation of skilled nursing home facilities, intermediate care facilities and residential facilities for the elderly. Management skills to select, train, motivate and develop staff. Skills to develop and maintain interpersonal relationships. Knowledge of the CCRC statutes. Sensitivity and understanding of the issues related to aging. Ability to make sound business decisions. Skill to synthesize a variety of information, consider alternatives and their consequences, formulate conclusions and recommend and implement actions. Sound budgeting development and implementation.
* Eight to ten years of major administrative experience and effective leadership of diverse team members. Previous experience in a similar senior living role. May be required to have or secure a license as a Nursing Home Administrator in California and a Residential Care Facility for the Elderly Certification.
* Full management responsibility for all staff (75 to 175\) activities. Manages directly or through subordinate supervisors. Responsible for recruitment, selection, training, motivation, discipline, and performance appraisal.


Who We Are:
Founded in 1958, Sequoia Living is a Bay Area\-based nonprofit organization dedicated to providing older adults with stimulating, joyful living environments and services that support and enrich their lives. Throughout our six decades as a nonprofit serving Bay Area seniors, we’ve learned the importance of connection and collaboration when it comes to providing resources for healthy aging. From our Life Plan Community to safe affordable housing, engaging senior centers, and a purpose\-filled volunteer program, we provide friendly environments where people can explore and discover what it means to grow stronger, wiser, and more joyful.  

Sequoia Living is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status. In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, Sequoia Living will provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities and encourage prospective employees to discuss potential accommodations with the employer.

Organization’s Mission: Sparking wonder through play, education, and nature to create a community of environmental stewards for a healthier Baltimore.  

  

Parks \& People works to sustain and improve Baltimore’s parks and open spaces through public\-private partnerships. Since 1984, P\&P has a history of making investments in green park projects to revitalize neighborhoods and is a major provider of programs to allow children, youth and adults to learn, grow, and explore their natural environment. Parks \& People envisions a Baltimore City where green renewal contributes to economic investment and population growth, where people enjoy green spaces that spark wonder, and where communities build the strength and leadership to steward the environment.  

  

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES: The Director of Development serves as Parks \& People’s chief development officer with oversight of the development department. Specifically, the Director of Development is responsible for leading a development team in the strategy and execution of fundraising work that results in raising $3\.5M in annual operating income through major giving activities, grants from public and private sector funders, and individual giving appeals. Therefore, this role requires an experienced development professional who can provide the expertise to create dynamic annual plans to realize the needed revenue target, and personally participate in the work required to generate needed income.  

  

The role manages a team, which currently consists of four full time equivalent staff persons (1\.5 FTE for communications, 1 FTE for Donor Relations, and 1\.5 FTEs for Grants prospecting, writing and reporting). The objective is to maximize P\&P fundraising potential and guide all its major functions to the next level of excellence, with the support of the aforementioned staff and CEO. The Director, working with the CEO, would be responsible for launching an endowment campaign, a planned giving process, planning and executing annual giving campaign, ensuring corporate and foundation grants and reports are completed, and developing and executing the strategy for sponsorships and donations at P\&P’s special events.  

  

REPORTS TO: President \& CEO  

  

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:  

  

 1\. Identify and cultivate major givers: This role includes identifying, engaging, and securing from current and prospective major gift donors at least $300K in annual operating support.  

 2\. Administer an outreach, communications and stewardship plan to establish and sustain relationships with current and prospective donors.

 4\. Manage Parks \& People’s development staff to ensure all fundraising efforts are performed well.

**Lead a fundraising program that's already working.**


KSPS PBS has served the Inland Northwest and Western Canada for nearly 60 years, connecting communities through trusted public media. We are looking for an experienced fundraiser and emerging or established leader to guide a strong, growing philanthropy program generating approximately $4\.8 million annually.


If you've looked at Development Director positions lately, you've probably seen some daunting ones.

**This is not a turnaround role, and you will not be expected to fundraise alone.**


You'll inherit an experienced eight\-person team, a deeply loyal donor base, a growing major gifts program, a maturing planned giving program, an endowment approaching $5 million, and fundraising performance that is already exceeding expectations.


You'll also have something every fundraiser deserves: **an executive team and board that understand fundraising is an organizational responsibility, not one person's job.**


Our Board of Directors participates in fundraising and maintains 100% board giving. Our President and General Manager spent three successful years leading this same development department and remains actively involved in donor cultivation and solicitation. The previous Development Director served for ten years.

**The position is open because of internal advancement, not turnover or poor performance.**


Our development team is tenured, growing, and delivering strong annual results. The foundation is here. Your job is to lead it into its next chapter.

**About KSPS PBS**


KSPS PBS is the public television station serving the Inland Northwest and Western Canada. Our philanthropy program includes membership and annual giving, major and planned giving, corporate underwriting, and development operations.


A note for candidates watching the public media landscape: with the 2025 loss of federal funding nationwide, some assume every public media organization is in financial distress.

**KSPS PBS is the counterexample.**


Our revenue has always come overwhelmingly from donors and community support, not federal dollars. KSPS PBS holds approximately $12\.1 million in total assets, $9\.3 million in net assets, and more than two years of liquid operating reserves. We have recorded five consecutive years of operating surpluses, and net assets have more than doubled since 2019\.


Our current fiscal year is running approximately 11% ahead of fundraising goals.


Don't take our word for it. Our Form 990s are public through ProPublica's Nonprofit Explorer under "Friends of KSPS," and we encourage candidates to look.

**The Opportunity**


The loss of approximately $1\.2 million in annual federal support created a significant challenge, but our community responded.


Supporters across the Inland Northwest and Western Canada have stepped forward in remarkable ways, substantially narrowing the resulting revenue gap. The next Director of Philanthropy \& Fundraising will help us retain and deepen those relationships while continuing a three\-year strategy to replace lost federal support with sustainable, diversified philanthropic revenue.

**We believe the goal is ambitious. We also believe it is achievable, and we have invested in the people, donor relationships, systems, reserves, and organizational support necessary to pursue it responsibly.**


Reporting to the President and General Manager, you'll lead an eight\-person development team responsible for membership, major and planned giving, corporate underwriting, and development operations.


This is both a leadership and frontline fundraising position, but it is not an expectation that the Director personally execute every fundraising function. **You are here to lead a capable team, develop strategy, build relationships, and personally engage where senior\-level involvement has the greatest impact.**

**In this role, you will:**

* Lead, coach, and support an experienced development team, setting clear goals while fostering accountability, collaboration, professional growth, and sustainable workloads.

The Regional Program Director is a member of the Roads to Freedom Center for Independent Living (RTFCIL) management team and provides leadership, oversight, and support for programs, staff, and operations within the assigned region.

The Regional Program Director focuses primarily on regional operations, staff leadership and support, program implementation, service delivery, organizational accountability, team development, quality improvement, and ensuring that services within the region remain strongly aligned with the Independent Living philosophy and the needs and direction of the disability community.

The Regional Program Director provides consistent leadership and supervision to regional managers, coordinators, and program staff and is responsible for ensuring employees have the direction, resources, support, training, and accountability necessary to successfully perform their responsibilities and provide high\-quality services.

Working closely with the Director of Compliance, Quality \& Risk Management and other members of organizational leadership, the Regional Program Director ensures that RTFCIL's strategic priorities, policies, programs, performance expectations, and organizational initiatives are effectively implemented throughout the region. The position also serves as an important communication link between regional staff and executive leadership by identifying operational needs, barriers, opportunities, emerging community needs, and areas requiring organizational attention.

The Director promotes an organizational culture that values consumer choice, self\-determination, dignity of risk, disability rights, peer support, community integration, staff development, collaboration, and accountability.

The primary function of the Regional Program Director is the effective internal management and performance of established RTFCIL programs, services, and regional staff. * Understanding the Independent Living philosophy and disability rights.
* Familiarity with CILSuite or similar service tracking and data management systems.

* Three or more years of supervisory or management experience in human services, preferably within a Center for Independent Living or disability services.

* Perform other related duties as assigned.

* Experience managing a portfolio of donors, including personally identifying, cultivating, and soliciting five\- and six\-figure gifts.
* Proficiency in Salesforce or similar CRM database.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

**Job Title: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**


**Department:** Administration

  

**FLSA Classification:** Exempt  

**Employment Status:** Full\-Time  

  

**Location:** Harrison County Community Hospital (HCCH)  

**Reports to:** Board of Directors

 **Job Summary/Objective**



The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) serves as the Board of Directors' direct executive representative and is responsible for the overall administration, leadership, management, and operation of Harrison County Community Hospital. The CEO is granted the authority necessary to direct hospital activities and departments in accordance with Board policies, regulatory requirements, and applicable laws.



The CEO provides strategic leadership to ensure the delivery of safe, high\-quality patient care; financial stability; operational excellence; regulatory compliance; and organizational growth. The CEO works collaboratively with the Board of Directors, Medical Staff, employees, legal counsel, community stakeholders, and healthcare partners to advance the mission and vision of the organization.



The CEO is expected to lead with integrity, accountability, transparency, and sound judgment while maintaining the highest standards of confidentiality regarding organizational, financial, and personnel matters.

 **Essential Functions/Duties/Responsibilities**


* Serve as the chief executive officer and authorized administrative representative of the Board of Directors in the management and operation of the hospital.
* Develop, implement, and evaluate strategic plans that support the hospital's mission, vision, goals, and long\-term sustainability, including to remain an independent entity.
* Direct and oversee all operational, clinical, financial, and administrative functions of the hospital to ensure efficiency, effectiveness, and quality outcomes.
* Provide overall leadership to hospital departments and coordinate organizational activities to ensure the effective delivery of patient care and healthcare service programs.
* Lead organizational improvement initiatives that advance patient safety, quality outcomes, operational effectiveness, employee engagement, and patient satisfaction.
* Select, employ, supervise, develop, evaluate, discipline, and discharge hospital employees and agents in accordance with Board policies, applicable laws, and organizational procedures.
* Recruit, mentor, and hold executive leaders accountable for organizational performance, strategic objectives, quality outcomes, and financial results.
